subject.title: fix(codex): stop stale MCP child processes with revalidated SIGKILL escalation

question: Should the macOS Codex integration forcibly SIGKILL a scoped Computer Use MCP child that remains alive two seconds after SIGTERM, once identity checks still match?
rationale: The implementation is mechanically bounded, but forced termination changes the runtime recovery contract and the available proof does not exercise the supported Darwin app-server lifecycle.

options.title: Require Darwin proof and approve the contract
options.body: Keep the escalation only after a real macOS Codex app-server run shows the helper lifecycle and an owner confirms forced cleanup is intended.

options.title: Keep SIGTERM-only cleanup
options.body: Reject forced escalation if lingering helpers should instead be diagnosed or recovered by the Codex runtime itself.

options.title: Defer to a Codex-owned repair
options.body: Pause this PR and move the behavior to the owner surface if the upstream Codex lifecycle should own helper termination.

recommendation.title: Require Darwin proof and approve the contract
recommendation.body: Keep the escalation only after a real macOS Codex app-server run shows the helper lifecycle and an owner confirms forced cleanup is intended.

likelyOwner.reason: Current-main ownership could not be established without the required history and sibling-Codex source inspection.
